notes.title: Eredia 2 is now LIVE!
notes.notes:
I'll keep this short and simple so there's less reading and more gaming. Eredia 2 is now Live and available for purchase at a 30 percent launch discount!

And if you haven't had the chance to play the first game yet, now is the perfect opportunity to buy it at a ridiculous 85% discount, during the launch week of Eredia 2! Although it is not mandatory to do so, the two games are designed to be experienced one after the other. And players who have finished the first game are recommended to export their saves to Eredia 2.

How to export the save file:

-> Navigate to the Eredia: Diary of Heroes/www folder in your steam library.
-> Copy the ENTIRE 'save' folder
-> Navigate to the Eredia: The Great War/www folder in your steam library.
-> Paste the save folder here. 
-> Even though the entire save folder has been exported, you can only load up the file which was saved in the player's home in Miralia after completing the first game. It's necessary to copy the entire folder so that the global and config files do not get missed.

Please do remember while playing that this game was made by a single dev, and while I tried to eliminate as many of the bugs as I could find, if you do run into something, please report them in the discussions section. I will try to fix them as soon as I can.

Lastly, please write your honest review after giving the game a try. Your feedback is critical to the success of Eredia as a whole.

That's all. Cheers and happy gaming!
Rishi

notes.title: Two Days Away!
notes.notes:
Dear Potato Lovers,

The testing phase took a bit longer than expected, but I'm glad to announce that almost all of those annoying icky bugs have been squished. At the same time, I have some bad news, some good news, and some even better news.

The good news is that I have managed to enable cloud saves for both Eredia 1 and 2. The bad news is that steam achievements might be broken for Eredia 2. I'm at my wits end trying to get them to work, but it just didn't happen the same way it did for Eredia 1.

As for the better news, we finally have a release date, and it's 14th December 2023. I know it's just two days away, but I couldn't commit to a final release date without knowing that I've eliminated all the bugs, at least the ones that we'd discovered.

My one final advice to players would be to play Eredia 1 first, in case you haven't already. Even though it's not necessary to have an Eredia 1 save file to play the sequel, it's a direct continuation of the story right from where it left off, and it'll be a more enjoyable experience to play these games in order.

That's all! See you on 14th.

Cheers,
Rishi

notes.title: New Year, New Updates, New Discounts
notes.notes:
Happy New Year, Eredians!

With 2020 and 2021 being rather unproductive in terms of Eredia 2's development, 2022 was far better. By the end of the year, we were able to finish:

- Developing all the towns
- Creating all four guilds along with their contracts and goodies
- Almost all the planned side contracts
- 90% of the world map (excluding free-roam islands)
- 70% of the main story content

Now, the above figures make it quite transparent that the main story development is a bit lagging as compared to the rest of the progress (world building, side quests, etc.). This is because I have hit a creative roadblock with the main story towards the end, and the RMMV map limit restriction is not helping either. However, it shouldn't take too long since most of the heavy lifting has already been taken care of, and the final 2-3 month testing phase will begin after I finish developing the main storyline. 

In the meantime, for those of you who haven't had the chance to try out Eredia: Diary of Heroes already, we are now offering an 85% discount for the first time (same for Eva Reynes). 

See you soon on the other side!
Rishi

notes.title: Eredia 2 Q2 Progress Report
notes.notes:
Hello Eredians!

A small progress report to keep you all updated on what's going on:

- The world map is now 80% fleshed out. Most of the mapping has now been completed.
- The main story is about 65-70% complete.
- Ran into a roadblock due to the way the RMMV engine handles the map limit. Apparently, there is still no easy workaround for the 999 map limit. I'm still able to make room for the new maps by deleting the older E1 maps that won't be used in E2, it might pose a problem in E3 when transitioning between the two world maps. As always, I will look for a solution.
- A change of plan: I won't be releasing any more tester builds until I at least finish writing the main story. This is mostly to avoid the extra effort since I am changing a lot of things as I keep remodeling the game.
Expect something around the end of the year.

Cheers,
Rishi

notes.title: Happy New Year, Eredians!
notes.notes:
Greetings, earthlings!

Hope you enjoyed your holidays.

The beginning of a new year is an obvious time for making new promises. Personally, I had made too many new year's resolutions back in the day to know that these promises are, in fact, the most breakable.

That is why I'm not making any promises this year. Rather, I'll focus on what works: taking things one step at a time. And that is what I had been doing with Eredia 2, despite the lack of communication from my end, lately. At this stage, I'm happy to announce that the game is over 50% complete, and while there are certain variables, I should be able to release the game later this year depending on how things proceed.

I am also pleasantly surprised to see the renewed interest the community has in Eredia, and the level of support it receives even to this day. I have decided that it's time to post a few screenshots to show what has been happening behind the scenes.

notes.title: The Future of Eredia and Potatobrain Games
notes.notes:
Greetings to you RPG-loving Potatoes!

It has been almost six months since the release of Eredia: Diary of Heroes, the first installment in the Eredia series, and so far I'm pleasantly surprised by the amount of positive response I got, especially on Steam. There were a few hiccups along the way, but the wonderful community made sure to report flaws and bugs whenever they found them, and it helped me improve the game greatly.

Now, several players have already started asking about Eredia 2, and I haven't given a proper response on this topic, yet. Well, let's start with the bad news, first. 

I haven't started working on Eredia 2. Have I abandoned the project? HELL NO! But after finishing the first installment of Eredia, I decided that I'd challenge myself and make a non-RPG game because I have so many stories that cannot be told in a semi-medieval fantasy world. 

I have started working on a Suspense/Detective game which will have dark themes and hardcore difficulty. This game is not as immense as Eredia, but it'll have a lot more original art, CGs, and the other stuff that commercial games usually have, and I plan to finish it in another six to nine months. I'll be rolling out a separate post for this topic soon.

I plan to start developing Eredia 2 in early 2019, and the development cycle will take anywhere between 12 to 18 months. Multiple users also asked what they can expect from the game; but to be perfectly honest, I haven't laid out any detailed plans yet, but the Aegea-Caradith war will continue, the Dark Silver will play a more prominent role in the story, new characters will be introduced, betrayals, plot-twists and surprises will keep you at the edge of your seat, and Kenrad will, of course, continue being who he is. That's as much spoiler-free information I can give you right now.

There's one more good news I'd like to share before ending this post:

Potatobrain Games is now open to publishing requests (non-commercial games) for FREE.

Yup, you read that right. I'll be rolling out a detailed post about this on my website and on Steam, so stay connected!

Cheers!
Rishi

notes.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Shiny
notes.notes:
Dear Eredians,

As the title suggests, I got some good news, some bad news, and something shiny to top it off.

I don't want you to start reading the announcement with a frown, so let's start with the good.

Several bug fixes and content improvement have been made, including:

- Fixed some game breaking combos.

- Fixed a bug where you could travel to Kindar Tower even after it was locked.

- Fixed several passage issues, most notably in the Baveidel Swamps.

- Fixed a bug which caused the Annual Tournament to repeat itself upon completion.

- Fixed several bugs which caused the game to get stuck if certain party members were not added to the team before the fights.

- Fixed the bug which caused the black ram to not appear even after adopting it.

- Fixed the bug of Ivy's second character quest not appearing.

- Fixed the bug which caused the Serpent's dialogues to repeat even after completing that quest.

- Fixed some equipment categorization bugs.

- Fixed a bug which caused certain skills to not appear in the menu even after learning them.

- Fixed a few typos and improved the overall textual formatting in several parts of the game.

- Fixed a few more bugs that I forgot about. (Because I'm a lazy bum and I didn't note them down when I fixed them)

The bad news is: there won't be a Mac version, at least for now. It isn't difficult to port the game to Mac and other operating systems, but right now I can't find a way to properly encrypt the files and still make them executable in Mac, thus ending up creating several security issues. Never say never, though; as soon as I find a way to port my game to Mac while being able to protect my files at the same time, I'll get right back on it.

As for the shinies, Eredia is going on a 50% discount for an entire week -- our biggest discount till date.

Cheers!

notes.title: Eredia Release Announcement
notes.notes:
Good morning, good afternoon, good evening, ladies and gentlemen!

The kraken has been released!...Okay, I'll stop with the bad jokes, now.
My first commercial game, Eredia: The Diary of Heroes, has finally been released!

For those who are not familiar with our title, Eredia is a dark fantasy JRPG game set in a vast open world with over 50 hours of non-linear gameplay. It follows the life of Kenrad Krauser, a hunter trying to make the most of his opportunities in a war-ravaged world.

Eredia is available for purchase in Steam and itch.io.

Note: For now, only the Windows version is available. Mac and Linux versions will be available in approximately one month.

To all those who have supported me and have been a part of this wonderful journey: thank you.
